intro: At B2 you wrote full essays with a thesis, body paragraphs and a conclusion. Now you'll make an argument truly **coherent**, use other writers' ideas honestly (**paraphrase, quote and cite** them), and see exactly what an **IELTS Writing Task 2** essay needs for band 7. Your C1 tools (hedging, collocations and nominalisation) all come together here.
teachingNotes: Builds on b2-essay-writing; recap in one line, don't re-teach: introduction = paraphrase of the question + thesis; body paragraph = topic sentence → explanation → example; conclusion with no new ideas; counter-arguments with Some people argue that … However, … / While it is true that …, … / Admittedly, …, but …; IELTS Task 2 = at least 250 words in about 40 minutes, Task 2 carries more weight than Task 1, question types opinion / discussion / problem-solution. The chain gives the tools to use (and praise) in essays and paraphrases: c1-hedging (tend to, suggests not proves, one hedge is enough), c1-collocations (conduct research, pose a threat, have an impact on, a pressing concern), c1-nominalisation (rose sharply → a sharp rise in; noun + preposition). Explain jargon the first time in plain Indonesian: coherent (koheren: runtut dan nyambung), thesis statement (pernyataan sikap), evidence (bukti), rebuttal (bantahan), source (sumber), paraphrase (parafrase), quote (kutipan langsung), quotation marks (tanda kutip), citation (sitasi / rujukan dalam teks), reference list (daftar pustaka), reporting verb (kata kerja pelapor), plagiarism (plagiarisme), criterion (kriteria), band (skor IELTS).

Objective build-a-coherent. The thesis must answer the actual question: 'To what extent do you agree?' needs HOW FAR (I largely agree / I partly agree / I completely disagree), not background (Advertising is everywhere today) or an announcement (This essay will discuss …). One position from introduction to conclusion: no switching sides at the end; a mixed view is fine if it is stated from the start. One main idea per paragraph in four moves: topic sentence → explanation → example or evidence → link (a sentence tying the point back to the thesis: … therefore …). The coherence test: the thesis plus the first sentence of each paragraph should read like a summary of the essay. Counter-argument + rebuttal: concede fairly (Admittedly, … / Critics point out that …), then answer with a reason or evidence (This argument has some merit, but … / However, this view overlooks … / … does not take into account …), then link back. Conclusion restates the position and the main reasons; no new ideas or examples. Indonesian habit to name respectfully: many Indonesian texts build up to the main point and state it at the end (paragraf induktif), and school essays open with long background ('Di era globalisasi ini …'); English academic readers expect the point first (paragraf deduktif).

Objective paraphrase-and-reference, and the node's common error (copying a sentence without quotation marks or a reference → paraphrase in your own words and cite (Author, year)). Paraphrase = new words AND new structure, the same meaning (keep numbers, scope words like some/many and hedges like may/tend to), and STILL cited. Four steps: understand → close the source → write from memory → compare. Two failures: too close (patchwriting: synonyms swapped, same sentence shape) and changed meaning (may → will, many → all, suggests → proves). Technical terms, names, numbers and dates can stay. Quote = exact words in quotation marks + citation (+ page in APA); quote sparingly. Reporting verbs: argues (reasons for a view), claims (can sound as if the writer doubts it), states / notes (neutral), suggests (careful), found / reports (research results), points out (something true the writer accepts). APA 7th edition as ONE common style (Harvard, MLA, Chicago and IEEE also exist; always follow the department's or journal's guide): (Santoso, 2021) / Santoso (2021) found that …; two authors (Pratama & Lestari, 2022) / Pratama and Lestari (2022); three or more (Hidayat et al., 2020); quote with page (Santoso, 2021, p. 34); reference list at the end, A–Z by family name: Santoso, B. (2021). Title. Publisher. APA usually uses the past tense for a study's results (found); many writers use the present (argues): accept both, ask for consistency. Indonesian names: many people have one name; APA writes a one-word name in full; otherwise follow the name as printed in the source or the department guide. All names, titles, journals and figures in the lesson are invented for practice.

Plagiarism, explained plainly and without moralising: presenting someone else's words or ideas as your own, on purpose or not. It includes copying without quotation marks AND copying WITH a citation but without quotation marks (the reference credits the idea; the words are still the author's: quote them or paraphrase them properly), too-close paraphrases, an idea or figure without a citation, and translating a source (from Indonesian or any language) without citing it; running a text through a translation or 'paraphrasing' app doesn't make it yours. Name the school 'copas' (copy-paste) habit respectfully: at university it's treated seriously (similarity checkers such as Turnitin, failed assignments, rejected theses). Common knowledge (Jakarta is the capital of Indonesia) needs no citation. IELTS is different: no sources or references are expected (examples come from general knowledge or experience); partly or wholly plagiarised scripts and memorised essays are penalised, and words copied from the question are discounted.

Objective argumentative-essay, IELTS facts stated accurately (official key assessment criteria and the public Task 2 band descriptors, updated May 2023). Four criteria, equally weighted (25% each of the Task 2 score): Task Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy ('Task Achievement' is the Task 1 name). Band 7 in plain words: TR main parts of the prompt addressed, a clear and developed position, main ideas extended and supported (may over-generalise or lack focus); CC logically organised with clear progression, a range of cohesive devices incl. reference used flexibly (some over/under-use), paragraphs generally effective; LR enough range for some flexibility and precision, some less common or idiomatic items, awareness of style and collocation, only a few spelling / word-formation errors; GRA a variety of complex structures, grammar and punctuation generally well controlled, frequent error-free sentences. Question types (teachers' labels): opinion, discussion, problem-solution, advantages-disadvantages ('Do the advantages outweigh …?' needs a view), two-part / direct questions (answer both). Never give official band scores to a text: say at most 'would probably be around band 7'; only trained examiners score. When the learner writes a full essay: check the shape first (thesis answering the question, one idea per paragraph with a link, counter-argument + rebuttal, conclusion with no new ideas, at least 250 words, every part answered), then give one or two points per criterion.

Limits and style: A0–B2 grammar plus the chain (hedging, collocations, nominalisation). Keep other C1 structures out of examples: no inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive, impersonal passives ('It is argued that …'); 'It could be argued that …' is a phrase to remember. c1-cohesion is not in the chain: don't teach albeit / notwithstanding / the former, the latter here, but accept them if the learner uses them correctly. At C1 much is style: accept any thesis that clearly answers the question and any paraphrase that keeps the meaning, changes words and structure and cites the source; only mark clear cases wrong (no position, a copied or near-copied sentence, a changed meaning, a missing citation or year, the wrong criterion). British vs American: quotation marks / inverted commas, single vs double marks, organise / organize: both fine if consistent.

keyPoints.title: A coherent argument: one position, paragraphs that support it
keyPoints.explanation: Your thesis statement answers the question in one sentence in the introduction (To what extent …? → how far you agree). Each body paragraph has one main idea in four moves: topic sentence → explanation → example or evidence → a link back to the thesis. Show the strongest counter-argument fairly, then rebut it with a reason. The conclusion restates your position and main reasons, with no new ideas. Put the main point first, not at the end.

examples.en: I largely agree, since young children cannot easily tell an advert from entertainment.
examples.id: Sebagian besar saya setuju, karena anak kecil tidak mudah membedakan iklan dari hiburan.

examples.en: Flexible hours therefore benefit companies as well as their employees.
examples.id: Karena itu, jam kerja fleksibel menguntungkan perusahaan sekaligus karyawannya.

examples.en: This argument has some merit, but it does not justify making students pay everything.
examples.id: Argumen ini ada benarnya, tetapi tidak membenarkan mahasiswa harus membayar semuanya.

id.title: Argumen yang koheren: satu posisi, paragraf yang mendukungnya
id.explanation: Thesis statement-mu menjawab pertanyaan dalam satu kalimat di pembuka (To what extent …? → seberapa jauh kamu setuju). Setiap paragraf isi punya satu ide pokok dalam empat langkah: topic sentence → penjelasan → contoh atau bukti → kalimat yang mengaitkan kembali ke thesis. Tunjukkan kontra-argumen terkuat secara adil, lalu bantah dengan alasan. Penutup menyatakan lagi posisimu dan alasan utamanya, tanpa ide baru. Taruh poin utama di depan, bukan di akhir.

keyPoints.title: Paraphrase, quote and cite your sources
keyPoints.explanation: A paraphrase changes the words AND the sentence structure but keeps the meaning (numbers, some/many, may/tend to), and you still cite it. Steps: understand → close the source → write → compare. A quote uses the exact words in quotation marks. In APA (one common style): (Santoso, 2021) or Santoso (2021) found that …, with the page for a quote, and a reference list at the end. A citation does not make copied words OK without quotation marks.

examples.en: According to Santoso (2021), the desire for better pay is the main reason why many young people in Jakarta change employers.
examples.id: Menurut Santoso (2021), keinginan mendapat gaji lebih baik adalah alasan utama banyak anak muda di Jakarta berganti tempat kerja.

examples.en: Remote workers tend to report higher job satisfaction (Pratama & Lestari, 2022).
examples.id: Pekerja jarak jauh cenderung melaporkan kepuasan kerja yang lebih tinggi (Pratama & Lestari, 2022).

examples.en: Santoso, B. (2021). Young workers in the city. Nusantara Press.
examples.id: Contoh entri daftar pustaka APA untuk buku: nama keluarga, inisial, (tahun), judul, penerbit.

id.title: Memparafrasekan, mengutip dan menyitasi sumber
id.explanation: Parafrase mengubah kata-kata DAN struktur kalimat tetapi mempertahankan maknanya (angka, some/many, may/tend to), dan tetap kamu sitasi. Langkahnya: pahami → tutup sumbernya → tulis → bandingkan. Kutipan langsung memakai kata-kata persis di dalam tanda kutip. Dalam APA (salah satu gaya yang umum): (Santoso, 2021) atau Santoso (2021) found that …, dengan nomor halaman untuk kutipan, dan daftar pustaka di akhir. Sitasi tidak membuat kata-kata yang disalin jadi boleh tanpa tanda kutip.

keyPoints.title: IELTS Writing Task 2 at band 7
keyPoints.explanation: At least 250 words in about 40 minutes. Four criteria, 25% each: Task Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy. Band 7 in plain words: every main part of the question answered with a clear position throughout, well-developed ideas, logical paragraphs, a range of vocabulary with some less common items, and a variety of complex sentences, many of them error-free. Know the question type: opinion, discussion, problem–solution, advantages–disadvantages or two-part.

examples.en: To what extent do you agree or disagree?
examples.id: Sejauh mana kamu setuju atau tidak setuju? (tipe opini)

examples.en: Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
examples.id: Apakah kelebihan perkembangan ini lebih besar daripada kekurangannya? (tipe kelebihan–kekurangan)

examples.en: Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
examples.id: Mengapa ini terjadi? Apakah ini perkembangan yang positif atau negatif? (tipe dua pertanyaan)

id.title: IELTS Writing Task 2 di band 7
id.explanation: Minimal 250 kata dalam sekitar 40 menit. Empat kriteria, masing-masing 25%: Task Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy. Band 7 dengan bahasa sederhana: setiap bagian utama pertanyaan dijawab dengan posisi yang jelas dari awal sampai akhir, ide yang dikembangkan dengan baik, paragraf yang logis, kosakata yang beragam dengan beberapa kata yang kurang umum, dan variasi kalimat kompleks yang banyak di antaranya bebas kesalahan. Kenali tipe pertanyaannya: opini, diskusi, masalah–solusi, kelebihan–kekurangan atau dua pertanyaan.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write a thesis statement (one sentence) for this IELTS question: 'Some people think that all public universities in Indonesia should teach their courses in English. To what extent do you agree or disagree?'
expected: i partly agree because english-medium courses prepare students for international careers but subjects such as law and medicine are better taught in indonesian
i largely disagree since most students learn complex ideas more effectively in their own language
i strongly agree because teaching in english would help indonesian graduates compete in the global job market
guidedPractice.hint: Say HOW FAR you agree (I largely agree / I partly agree / I strongly disagree) and give the main reason. Not background (English is a global language) and not an announcement (This essay will discuss …).

guidedPractice.prompt: Put these sentences in the best order for one body paragraph. Write the letters. A: For example, in some villages in Bali, income from homestays now pays for local roads and schools. B: Community-based tourism can bring real income to rural areas. C: Tourism of this kind therefore supports the communities it depends on. D: When villagers run homestays and tours themselves, the money stays in the village instead of going to large hotel chains.
guidedPractice.hint: Topic sentence (the point) → explanation (why or how) → example or evidence (For example, …) → link back to the thesis (… therefore …).

guidedPractice.prompt: Paraphrase this source sentence in your own words and cite it in APA style: 'Online learning may widen the gap between students in cities and those in rural areas.' (Rahmawati, 2022)
expected: according to rahmawati 2022 the difference between urban and rural students could grow larger as more teaching moves online
rahmawati 2022 suggests that the move to online classes might increase the inequality between students in towns and in the countryside
the shift to online learning could make the divide between urban and rural students wider rahmawati 2022
guidedPractice.hint: Understand it, cover it, write it from memory, then compare. Change the words AND the structure (widen the gap → make the divide wider / increase the inequality). Keep the hedge: may → could / might, not will. Add (Rahmawati, 2022) or start with Rahmawati (2022) suggests that …

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the APA in-text citation in brackets for a 2020 article by three authors: Hidayat, Siregar and Nugroho.
guidedPractice.hint: With three or more authors, APA gives the first family name + et al. (= dan kawan-kawan), then a comma and the year: (Hidayat et al., 2020).

guidedPractice.prompt: Which IELTS Task 2 question type is this? 'More and more people in Indonesia are shopping through social media apps. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?' Write opinion, discussion, problem-solution, advantages-disadvantages or two-part.
guidedPractice.hint: 'Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?' asks you to weigh both sides AND say which side is bigger: that's your position.

independentPractice.prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 (about 40 minutes, at least 250 words). 'Some people believe that the best way to reduce traffic congestion in big cities is to make public transport free. To what extent do you agree or disagree?' Plan for 5 minutes first: your position, one main idea per body paragraph, and the counter-argument you will answer.
expected: this argument has some merit but
independentPractice.hint: Rubric (the four criteria, 25% each). Task Response: a thesis that says how far you agree, kept from start to end; every idea developed with an explanation and an example; at least 250 words. Coherence and Cohesion: one main idea per paragraph (topic sentence → explanation → example → link); a counter-argument and a rebuttal; a conclusion with no new ideas. Lexical Resource: precise vocabulary and correct collocations (ease congestion, pose a problem, have an impact on), some less common words, few spelling errors. Grammatical Range and Accuracy: a mix of simple and complex sentences (conditionals, relative clauses, nominalisation), many of them error-free. No references needed: support ideas with reasons and general examples.

independentPractice.prompt: Use this source in a paragraph about flooding in Jakarta: 'Land subsidence, caused largely by the extraction of groundwater, has made parts of northern Jakarta increasingly vulnerable to flooding' (Wibowo, 2023, p. 12). Write (1) one sentence that paraphrases it with an in-text citation, (2) one sentence that quotes a short phrase from it, and (3) the reference list entry for a 2023 book by Dimas Wibowo called 'Cities below sea level', published by Nusantara Press.
expected: wibowo 2023 explains that because so much groundwater is pumped out the land in north jakarta is sinking and this makes floods more likely
wibowo 2023 describes parts of northern jakarta as increasingly vulnerable to flooding p 12
wibowo d 2023 cities below sea level nusantara press
independentPractice.hint: (1) New words and new structure (extraction of groundwater → pumping out groundwater; increasingly vulnerable → more and more at risk), same meaning, cited. (2) Exact words inside quotation marks + the page: Wibowo (2023) describes … as "increasingly vulnerable to flooding" (p. 12). (3) Wibowo, D. (2023). Cities below sea level. Nusantara Press. (book title in italics).

independentPractice.prompt: Your essay argues that schools in Indonesia should start lessons later in the morning. Write a counter-argument paragraph of 3–4 sentences: present the strongest view against you fairly, rebut it with a reason, and link back to your thesis.
expected: admittedly a later start would make it harder for some parents to drop their children off on the way to work
this argument has some merit but
independentPractice.hint: 1. Concede: Admittedly, … / Critics point out that … 2. Rebut: This argument has some merit, but … / However, this view overlooks … (+ a reason or evidence). 3. Link: … therefore, a later start would still … Answer the idea, not the people; hedge where the evidence is limited (may, tend to).

assessment.prompt: This body paragraph comes from an essay arguing that cities should plant more trees. Which sentence breaks the 'one main idea' rule and should be removed? Write its number. (1) Trees can make city streets noticeably cooler. (2) Their shade blocks direct sunlight, so roads and buildings absorb less heat. (3) Many residents of Surabaya also enjoy jogging in the city's parks in the morning. (4) For example, tree-lined streets in Surabaya tend to feel much cooler on hot afternoons than open roads nearby. (5) Planting more trees is therefore one of the cheapest ways to make a city more comfortable.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 3 (jogging in parks is a different idea, exercise and leisure; the paragraph's main idea is that trees keep streets cool). 1 = 0 (the topic sentence). 2 = 0 (the explanation). 4 = 0 (the example). 5 = 0 (the link back to the thesis).

assessment.prompt: In an argumentative essay, the writer first presents the strongest view against their own position. What do we call the writer's answer to it, the part that shows why that view is weaker? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: rebuttal (or refutation) = bantahan. 'response' / 'answer' / 'reply' = 30 (the right idea, but not the term). 'counter-argument' / 'counterargument' = 0 (that's the opposing view itself). 'thesis' / 'conclusion' / 'concession' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rina's essay ends with this APA reference list entry for a journal article. One essential part is missing. What is it? 'Pratama, A. Remote work and job satisfaction in Jakarta. Indonesian Journal of Work Studies, 12(2), 45–60. https://doi.org/10.1234/ijws.12.2.45'
assessment.rubric: Correct: the year (of publication), in brackets after the author: Pratama, A. (2022). Without it, the in-text citation (Pratama, 2022) can't be matched to the entry. 'author' / 'title' / 'journal name' / 'pages' / 'volume' / 'DOI' = 0 (all already there). 'the publisher' = 0 (journal articles in APA don't list one).

assessment.prompt: Complete the paraphrase with ONE noun. Source: 'House prices in Bali rose sharply between 2015 and 2020' (Putra, 2021). Paraphrase: 'Putra (2021) reports a sharp ___ in Balinese house prices between 2015 and 2020.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: rise / increase (nominalisation: rose sharply → a sharp rise in; jump is also natural). 'growth' = 60 (right meaning, but 'a sharp growth in' is unusual: growth is normally used without 'a'). 'rising' / 'raise' / 'rose' = 20 (not the noun: a raise is a pay rise in American English). 'fall' / 'decrease' = 0 (changes the meaning).

assessment.prompt: Sari wants to use six exact words from a report in her thesis, together with a citation and the page number. What punctuation must go around those words? Write two words.
assessment.rubric: Correct: quotation marks (British also: inverted commas). Exact words always need them, even with a citation; otherwise it's plagiarism of the wording. 'brackets' / 'parentheses' = 0 (those go around the citation, not the quoted words). 'italics' = 0. 'commas' = 0.

assessment.prompt: An examiner's comment on Budi's IELTS Writing Task 2 essay: 'Wide range of vocabulary, accurate complex sentences and clear paragraphs. However, the question asked whether the advantages of online shopping outweigh the disadvantages, and the essay only lists advantages and never gives the writer's view.' Which of the four criteria does this weakness affect most? Write its name.
assessment.rubric: Correct: Task Response (not answering every part of the question, with no clear position). 'Task Achievement' = 50 (that's the Task 1 name for the same idea). 'Coherence and Cohesion' = 10 (organisation and linking were fine). 'Lexical Resource' / 'Grammatical Range and Accuracy' = 0 (the comment praises vocabulary and grammar).

assessment.prompt: Dimas writes an IELTS Writing Task 2 essay of 231 words. At least how many more words does he need to reach the minimum length? Write the number.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 19 (the minimum is 250 words; 250 − 231 = 19). '250' = 30 (the minimum itself, not how many more). '69' = 20 (300 is a sensible target, not the minimum). Any number based on 150 (the Task 1 minimum) = 0.

material.title: A coherent argument: one position, every paragraph supporting it

id.title: Argumen yang koheren: satu posisi, setiap paragraf mendukungnya

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B2: an essay has an **introduction** (the question in your own words + your thesis), **body paragraphs** (one main idea each) and a **conclusion** (no new ideas), and you answer the other side with *However, …* or *While it is true that …*.

At C1 the question is: does it all hang together? A **coherent** argument (*koheren*: runtut dan nyambung) lets the reader follow one clear line of thinking from the first sentence to the last.

1. **A thesis statement that answers the question.** The **thesis** (*pernyataan sikap*) is your answer in one sentence, in the introduction. Read the question carefully: *To what extent do you agree?* needs **how far** you agree (*I largely agree*, *I partly agree*, *I strongly disagree*), not background and not an announcement like *This essay will discuss …*.
2. **One main idea per paragraph**, in four moves: **topic sentence** (the point) → **explanation** (why or how) → **example or evidence** (*bukti*: a fact, a number, a study, a real case) → **link** (one sentence that ties the point back to your thesis).
3. **The other side and your rebuttal.** A **counter-argument** is the strongest view against you; the **rebuttal** (*bantahan*) answers it with a reason or evidence: *Admittedly, … This argument has some merit, but …* / *However, this view overlooks …* (*mengabaikan*).
4. **A conclusion that restates.** Your position again in new words and your main reasons in short. **No new ideas, no new examples.**

A quick test: read only your thesis and the first sentence of each paragraph. If that reads like a summary of the whole essay, it's coherent.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B2: esai punya **pembuka** (pertanyaannya dengan kata-katamu sendiri + thesis-mu), **paragraf isi** (masing-masing satu ide pokok) dan **penutup** (tanpa ide baru), dan kamu menjawab sisi sebaliknya dengan *However, …* atau *While it is true that …*.

Di C1 pertanyaannya: apakah semuanya menyatu? Argumen yang **koheren** (*coherent*: runtut dan nyambung) membuat pembaca bisa mengikuti satu alur pikiran yang jelas dari kalimat pertama sampai terakhir.

1. **Thesis statement yang menjawab pertanyaan.** **Thesis** (pernyataan sikap) adalah jawabanmu dalam satu kalimat, di pembuka. Baca pertanyaannya dengan teliti: *To what extent do you agree?* meminta **seberapa jauh** kamu setuju (*I largely agree*, *I partly agree*, *I strongly disagree*), bukan latar belakang dan bukan pengumuman seperti *This essay will discuss …*.
2. **Satu ide pokok per paragraf**, dalam empat langkah: **topic sentence** (intinya) → **penjelasan** (kenapa atau bagaimana) → **contoh atau bukti** (*evidence*: fakta, angka, penelitian, kasus nyata) → **link** (satu kalimat yang mengaitkan poinnya kembali ke thesis-mu).
3. **Sisi sebaliknya dan bantahanmu.** **Counter-argument** (kontra-argumen) adalah pandangan terkuat yang berlawanan denganmu; **rebuttal** (bantahan) menjawabnya dengan alasan atau bukti: *Admittedly, … This argument has some merit, but …* / *However, this view overlooks …* (mengabaikan).
4. **Penutup yang menegaskan ulang.** Posisimu lagi dengan kata-kata baru dan alasan utamamu secara singkat. **Tanpa ide baru, tanpa contoh baru.**

Tes cepat: baca hanya thesis-mu dan kalimat pertama setiap paragraf. Kalau itu terbaca seperti ringkasan seluruh esai, esaimu koheren.

rows.en: I believe that companies should offer flexible working hours wherever the job allows it.
rows.id: Saya yakin perusahaan sebaiknya menawarkan jam kerja fleksibel di mana pun pekerjaannya memungkinkan.

id.note: thesis (di pembuka)

rows.en: The strongest argument for flexible hours is that they cut the time workers waste in traffic.
rows.id: Argumen terkuat untuk jam fleksibel adalah jam fleksibel memangkas waktu yang terbuang pekerja di jalan.

id.note: 1 topic sentence: intinya

rows.en: Staff who start at seven or at ten avoid the worst rush hour, so they arrive less tired and work better.
rows.id: Staf yang mulai jam tujuh atau jam sepuluh menghindari jam sibuk terparah, jadi mereka tiba tidak terlalu lelah dan bekerja lebih baik.

id.note: 2 penjelasan: kenapa atau bagaimana

rows.en: For example, at Rina's office in Jakarta, staff saved about 40 minutes a day after flexible start times were introduced.
rows.id: Contohnya, di kantor Rina di Jakarta, staf menghemat sekitar 40 menit sehari setelah jam mulai fleksibel diberlakukan.

id.note: 3 contoh atau bukti

rows.en: Flexible hours therefore benefit companies as well as their employees.
rows.id: Karena itu, jam kerja fleksibel menguntungkan perusahaan sekaligus karyawannya.

id.note: 4 link: kembali ke thesis

blocks.text:
**Main point first.** Many Indonesian texts build up to the main point and state it at the end (*paragraf induktif*), and school essays often open with long background (*Di era globalisasi ini …*). English academic readers expect the opposite: your position in the introduction, and the main idea at the **start** of each paragraph. If the reader has to wait until the conclusion to find out what you think, the essay isn't coherent for them.

**Don't switch sides.** An essay that says *I agree* in the introduction and *both sides have good arguments* in the conclusion has lost its line. If your view is mixed, say so from the start: *I partly agree: …*

id.text:
**Poin utama di depan.** Banyak teks berbahasa Indonesia membangun alur menuju poin utama dan baru menyatakannya di akhir (paragraf induktif), dan esai sekolah sering dibuka dengan latar belakang panjang (*Di era globalisasi ini …*). Pembaca akademik berbahasa Inggris mengharapkan kebalikannya: posisimu di pembuka, dan ide pokok di **awal** setiap paragraf. Kalau pembaca harus menunggu sampai penutup untuk tahu pendapatmu, esainya tidak koheren bagi mereka.

**Jangan pindah sisi.** Esai yang bilang *I agree* di pembuka lalu *both sides have good arguments* di penutup sudah kehilangan alurnya. Kalau pandanganmu campuran, katakan dari awal: *I partly agree: …*

blocks.prompt: The thesis of an essay is: 'Companies should stop printing documents wherever possible.' Which sentence is a link sentence that ties a body paragraph back to it?
options: Many offices in Jakarta still print every document.
Going paperless therefore saves companies money as well as protecting the environment.
For example, one bank in Surabaya cut its paper use by half in a year.
blocks.explain: A **link** sentence closes the paragraph and connects its point to the thesis: **therefore** + *going paperless saves money* points straight back to *stop printing documents*. The first sentence is background, and the *For example* sentence is evidence: it supports the point but doesn't tie it back.

id.prompt: Tesis sebuah esai: 'Companies should stop printing documents wherever possible.' Kalimat mana yang menjadi link sentence, yang mengaitkan paragraf isi kembali ke tesis itu?
id.explain: Kalimat **link** menutup paragraf dan menghubungkan poinnya ke thesis: **therefore** + *going paperless saves money* langsung merujuk kembali ke *stop printing documents*. Kalimat pertama hanya latar belakang, dan kalimat *For example* adalah bukti: mendukung poinnya tapi tidak mengaitkannya kembali.

material.title: A model IELTS Task 2 essay, paragraph by paragraph

id.title: Contoh esai IELTS Task 2, paragraf demi paragraf

blocks.text:
Here's an IELTS-style opinion question and a model answer of about 320 words. Read it to see the shape and the language, **not to memorise it**: examiners recognise memorised essays, and the band descriptors treat memorised language as a weakness.

We haven't given it a band score: only trained IELTS examiners give official scores. It was written to show the features the band 7 descriptions talk about: a clear position all the way through, developed ideas, a counter-argument with a rebuttal, and a conclusion with no new ideas.

**The question:** *Some people believe that university students should pay the full cost of their studies, because they are the ones who benefit most. To what extent do you agree or disagree?*

id.text:
Ini pertanyaan opini gaya IELTS dan contoh jawaban sekitar 320 kata. Bacalah untuk melihat bentuk dan bahasanya, **bukan untuk dihafal**: penguji mengenali esai hafalan, dan band descriptors menganggap bahasa hafalan sebagai kelemahan.

Kami tidak memberinya skor band: hanya penguji IELTS terlatih yang memberi skor resmi. Esai ini ditulis untuk menunjukkan ciri-ciri yang disebut dalam deskripsi band 7: posisi yang jelas dari awal sampai akhir, ide yang dikembangkan, kontra-argumen dengan bantahan, dan penutup tanpa ide baru.

**Pertanyaannya:** *Some people believe that university students should pay the full cost of their studies, because they are the ones who benefit most. To what extent do you agree or disagree?* (Sebagian orang yakin mahasiswa sebaiknya membayar seluruh biaya kuliahnya, karena merekalah yang paling diuntungkan. Sejauh mana kamu setuju atau tidak setuju?)

rows.en: In many countries, including Indonesia, the rising cost of higher education has become a pressing concern for families. Some people believe that students should pay the full cost of their degrees, since graduates tend to earn more than people without a degree. While I accept that graduates gain a great deal from their studies, I largely disagree, because society as a whole also benefits from a well-educated population.
rows.id: Di banyak negara, termasuk Indonesia, biaya pendidikan tinggi yang terus naik sudah menjadi kekhawatiran mendesak bagi keluarga. Sebagian orang yakin mahasiswa sebaiknya membayar seluruh biaya kuliahnya, karena lulusan cenderung berpenghasilan lebih tinggi daripada orang tanpa gelar. Walaupun saya menerima bahwa lulusan mendapat banyak manfaat dari kuliahnya, sebagian besar saya tidak setuju, karena masyarakat secara keseluruhan juga mendapat manfaat dari penduduk yang berpendidikan baik.
rows.note: introduction: the topic in new words + the thesis (I largely disagree, because …)

id.note: pembuka: topiknya dengan kata-kata baru + thesis (I largely disagree, because …)

rows.en: The main reason for public funding is that the benefits of higher education reach far beyond the individual. Doctors, teachers and engineers provide services that everyone depends on, and a well-educated workforce tends to attract investment and create jobs. For example, the growth of Indonesia's digital economy relies heavily on graduates with skills in technology and data. If students had to cover the full cost, many young people from low-income families would not be able to study, and the country would lose a great deal of talent. For this reason, public money spent on universities is better seen as an investment than as a cost.
rows.id: Alasan utama untuk dana publik adalah manfaat pendidikan tinggi jauh melampaui individu. Dokter, guru dan insinyur memberikan layanan yang diandalkan semua orang, dan tenaga kerja yang berpendidikan baik cenderung menarik investasi dan menciptakan lapangan kerja. Contohnya, pertumbuhan ekonomi digital Indonesia sangat bergantung pada lulusan yang punya keterampilan teknologi dan data. Kalau mahasiswa harus menanggung seluruh biayanya, banyak anak muda dari keluarga berpenghasilan rendah tidak akan bisa kuliah, dan negara akan kehilangan banyak sekali talenta. Karena itu, uang publik yang dipakai untuk universitas lebih tepat dilihat sebagai investasi daripada sebagai biaya.
rows.note: body 1: topic sentence → explanation → example → link (For this reason, …)

id.note: isi 1: topic sentence → penjelasan → contoh → link (For this reason, …)

rows.en: Admittedly, government budgets are limited, and money spent on universities cannot be used for hospitals or schools. Critics also point out that graduates usually earn higher salaries over their lifetime, so it seems fair for them to contribute. This argument has some merit, but it does not justify making students pay everything. A fairer approach is a system in which students pay part of their fees according to their family's income, as the single tuition fee (UKT) system at Indonesian state universities is designed to do. In this way, families who can afford more pay more, while talented students from poorer backgrounds are not excluded.
rows.id: Memang harus diakui anggaran pemerintah terbatas, dan uang yang dipakai untuk universitas tidak bisa dipakai untuk rumah sakit atau sekolah. Para pengkritik juga menunjukkan bahwa lulusan biasanya berpenghasilan lebih tinggi sepanjang hidupnya, jadi tampaknya adil kalau mereka ikut membayar. Argumen ini ada benarnya, tetapi tidak membenarkan mahasiswa harus membayar semuanya. Pendekatan yang lebih adil adalah sistem di mana mahasiswa membayar sebagian biayanya sesuai penghasilan keluarganya, seperti tujuan sistem uang kuliah tunggal (UKT) di perguruan tinggi negeri di Indonesia. Dengan begitu, keluarga yang mampu membayar lebih akan membayar lebih, sementara mahasiswa berbakat dari keluarga kurang mampu tidak tersingkir.
rows.note: body 2: the counter-argument (Admittedly, … Critics also point out …), then the rebuttal (This argument has some merit, but …)

id.note: isi 2: kontra-argumen (Admittedly, … Critics also point out …), lalu bantahannya (This argument has some merit, but …)

rows.en: In conclusion, although graduates clearly benefit from a degree, I do not believe that they should carry the whole financial burden. Since society also gains from their knowledge and skills, sharing the cost between students and the state is the fairest solution.
rows.id: Kesimpulannya, walaupun lulusan jelas mendapat manfaat dari gelarnya, saya tidak yakin mereka sebaiknya menanggung seluruh beban biayanya. Karena masyarakat juga mendapat manfaat dari pengetahuan dan keterampilan mereka, membagi biaya antara mahasiswa dan negara adalah solusi yang paling adil.
rows.note: conclusion: the position again + the main reason, nothing new

id.note: penutup: posisinya lagi + alasan utamanya, tanpa hal baru

blocks.text:
**What to notice:**
- The thesis answers *to what extent*: **I largely disagree**, with the reason. The conclusion says the same thing in new words.
- The counter-argument is stated fairly before it's answered, and the rebuttal gives a reason (a fairer system exists), not an attack on people.
- Your C1 tools: **hedging** (*tend to, usually, it seems fair*), **collocations** (*a pressing concern, relies heavily on, carry the whole financial burden*), **nominalisation** (*the rising cost of higher education, the growth of Indonesia's digital economy*).
- **No references.** An IELTS essay doesn't cite sources: you can't look anything up in the exam, so you support ideas with reasons and general examples. A university essay on the same topic would cite research for each claim.

id.text:
**Yang perlu diperhatikan:**
- Thesis-nya menjawab *to what extent*: **I largely disagree**, beserta alasannya. Penutupnya mengatakan hal yang sama dengan kata-kata baru.
- Kontra-argumennya disampaikan secara adil sebelum dijawab, dan bantahannya memberi alasan (ada sistem yang lebih adil), bukan menyerang orang.
- Alat-alat C1-mu: **hedging** (*tend to, usually, it seems fair*), **kolokasi** (*a pressing concern, relies heavily on, carry the whole financial burden*), **nominalisasi** (*the rising cost of higher education, the growth of Indonesia's digital economy*).
- **Tanpa daftar pustaka.** Esai IELTS tidak menyitasi sumber: kamu tidak bisa mencari apa pun saat ujian, jadi kamu mendukung ide dengan alasan dan contoh umum. Esai kuliah dengan topik yang sama akan menyitasi penelitian untuk setiap klaim.

blocks.prompt: In the model essay, which sentence is the rebuttal (the writer's answer to the other side)?
options: Admittedly, government budgets are limited, and money spent on universities cannot be used for hospitals or schools.
This argument has some merit, but it does not justify making students pay everything.
In conclusion, although graduates clearly benefit from a degree, I do not believe that they should carry the whole financial burden.
blocks.explain: **This argument has some merit, but …** accepts part of the other side and then answers it: that's the rebuttal. The *Admittedly* sentence presents the counter-argument (it agrees with the other side), and the *In conclusion* sentence restates the writer's position at the end.

id.prompt: Di contoh esai, kalimat mana yang menjadi bantahan (rebuttal: jawaban penulis terhadap sisi sebaliknya)?
id.explain: **This argument has some merit, but …** menerima sebagian sisi sebaliknya lalu menjawabnya: itulah bantahannya. Kalimat *Admittedly* menyampaikan kontra-argumennya (setuju dengan sisi sebaliknya), dan kalimat *In conclusion* menegaskan ulang posisi penulis di akhir.

blocks.text:
When you use a **source** (*sumber*: a book, an article, a report, a website), you have two honest choices:
- **Paraphrase** (*parafrase*): the idea in **your own words AND your own sentence structure**, with the **same meaning**. You still **cite** the source, because the idea isn't yours.
- **Quote** (*kutipan langsung*): the **exact words**, inside **quotation marks** ("…"), with a citation. Use quotes for a short phrase that is special or that you want to discuss, not for whole paragraphs.

**Paraphrasing in four steps:**
1. **Understand**: read the passage until you could explain it to a friend.
2. **Close the source**: put it away or cover it.
3. **Write** the idea from memory, in your own words and structure.
4. **Compare**: check the meaning is the same (numbers, *some / many*, hedges like *may* or *tend to*) and that you haven't copied a string of words. Then add the citation.

**Two ways a paraphrase fails:**
- **Too close**: you swap a few words for synonyms but keep the sentence shape (*patchwriting*, menambal kata). It's still copying, even with a citation.
- **The meaning changes**: you add, drop or strengthen something. If the source says *may* and you write *will*, or *many* becomes *all*, it's no longer the author's claim.

Your C1 tools help: **nominalisation** changes the structure (*want a higher salary* → *the desire for better pay*), **collocations** keep the new words natural, and **hedges** must stay exactly as strong or as weak as in the source.

id.text:
Saat kamu memakai **sumber** (*source*: buku, artikel, laporan, situs web), ada dua pilihan yang jujur:
- **Parafrase** (*paraphrase*): idenya dengan **kata-katamu sendiri DAN struktur kalimatmu sendiri**, dengan **makna yang sama**. Kamu tetap **menyitasi** sumbernya, karena idenya bukan milikmu.
- **Kutipan langsung** (*quote*): **kata-kata persisnya**, di dalam **tanda kutip** ("…"), dengan sitasi. Pakai kutipan untuk frasa pendek yang istimewa atau yang ingin kamu bahas, bukan untuk paragraf utuh.

**Memparafrasekan dalam empat langkah:**
1. **Pahami**: baca bagian itu sampai kamu bisa menjelaskannya ke teman.
2. **Tutup sumbernya**: singkirkan atau tutupi.
3. **Tulis** idenya dari ingatan, dengan kata-kata dan strukturmu sendiri.
4. **Bandingkan**: cek maknanya sama (angka, *some / many*, pelunak seperti *may* atau *tend to*) dan kamu tidak menyalin rangkaian kata. Lalu tambahkan sitasinya.

**Dua cara parafrase gagal:**
- **Terlalu mirip**: kamu mengganti beberapa kata dengan sinonim tapi bentuk kalimatnya tetap (*patchwriting*, menambal kata). Itu tetap menyalin, walaupun ada sitasinya.
- **Maknanya berubah**: kamu menambah, membuang atau memperkuat sesuatu. Kalau sumbernya bilang *may* lalu kamu tulis *will*, atau *many* jadi *all*, itu bukan lagi klaim penulisnya.

Alat-alat C1-mu membantu: **nominalisasi** mengubah strukturnya (*want a higher salary* → *the desire for better pay*), **kolokasi** membuat kata-kata barunya tetap alami, dan **pelunak** (hedges) harus tetap sama kuat atau sama lemahnya seperti di sumber.

rows.en: Many young employees in Jakarta leave their first job within two years, mainly because they want a higher salary.
rows.id: Banyak karyawan muda di Jakarta meninggalkan pekerjaan pertama mereka dalam dua tahun, terutama karena mereka ingin gaji yang lebih tinggi.

id.note: sumbernya (Santoso, 2021, hlm. 34)

rows.en: Many young workers in Jakarta quit their first job within two years, mostly because they want a higher salary (Santoso, 2021).
rows.id: Banyak pekerja muda di Jakarta keluar dari pekerjaan pertama mereka dalam dua tahun, sebagian besar karena mereka ingin gaji yang lebih tinggi (Santoso, 2021).
rows.note: ✗ too close: three words swapped, same shape; the citation doesn't save it

id.note: ✗ terlalu mirip: tiga kata diganti, bentuknya sama; sitasinya tidak menyelamatkannya

rows.en: Santoso (2021) shows that all young people in Jakarta leave their jobs because of money.
rows.id: Santoso (2021) menunjukkan bahwa semua anak muda di Jakarta keluar dari pekerjaannya karena uang.
rows.note: ✗ meaning changed: many → all, mainly → only money, the two years are gone

id.note: ✗ maknanya berubah: many → all, mainly → hanya uang, dua tahunnya hilang

rows.en: According to Santoso (2021), the desire for better pay is the main reason why a large number of young people in Jakarta change employers during their first two years of work.
rows.id: Menurut Santoso (2021), keinginan mendapat gaji lebih baik adalah alasan utama banyak anak muda di Jakarta berganti tempat kerja dalam dua tahun pertama mereka bekerja.
rows.note: ✓ paraphrase: new words, new structure, same meaning, cited

id.note: ✓ parafrase: kata baru, struktur baru, makna sama, disitasi

rows.en: Santoso (2021) notes that young employees often leave "mainly because they want a higher salary" (p. 34).
rows.id: Santoso (2021) mencatat bahwa karyawan muda sering keluar "terutama karena mereka ingin gaji yang lebih tinggi" (hlm. 34).
rows.note: ✓ quote: exact words in quotation marks + the page

id.note: ✓ kutipan: kata-kata persis dalam tanda kutip + halamannya

blocks.text:
**What you can keep:** technical terms (*minimum wage, greenhouse gas*), names, numbers and dates. Changing them would change the meaning, so they stay.

**Quotation marks:** American English and APA use double marks ("…"); British English often uses single marks ('…') and also calls them *inverted commas*. Either way, the words inside are exactly the source's words.

**The translation trap:** translating an Indonesian source into English does **not** make it your own words: the idea and the wording plan are still the author's, so cite it. Running a text through a translation or 'paraphrasing' app doesn't make it yours either, and it often changes the meaning.

id.text:
**Yang boleh tetap:** istilah teknis (*minimum wage, greenhouse gas*), nama, angka dan tanggal. Mengubahnya justru mengubah makna, jadi biarkan tetap.

**Tanda kutip:** bahasa Inggris Amerika dan APA memakai tanda kutip ganda ("…"); bahasa Inggris Britania sering memakai tanda kutip tunggal ('…') dan juga menyebutnya *inverted commas*. Apa pun bentuknya, kata-kata di dalamnya persis kata-kata sumber.

**Jebakan terjemahan:** menerjemahkan sumber berbahasa Indonesia ke bahasa Inggris **tidak** membuatnya jadi kata-katamu sendiri: ide dan susunan pikirannya tetap milik penulis, jadi sitasi sumbernya. Memasukkan teks ke aplikasi terjemahan atau 'parafrase' juga tidak membuatnya jadi milikmu, dan sering malah mengubah maknanya.

blocks.prompt: Source: 'Rice prices may rise before Lebaran' (Kusuma, 2024). Which paraphrase keeps the meaning?
options: Kusuma (2024) predicts that the price of rice will rise before Lebaran.
Kusuma (2024) suggests that the price of rice could go up ahead of Lebaran.
Rice prices may rise before Lebaran.
blocks.explain: The source is careful (**may**), so the paraphrase must be careful too: **suggests … could go up** keeps that, with new words and a citation. *will rise* turns a possibility into a prediction: the meaning changes. The last option copies the source word for word with no quotation marks and no citation.

id.prompt: Sumber: 'Rice prices may rise before Lebaran' (Kusuma, 2024). Parafrase mana yang mempertahankan maknanya?
id.explain: Sumbernya berhati-hati (**may**), jadi parafrasenya juga harus berhati-hati: **suggests … could go up** mempertahankannya, dengan kata-kata baru dan sitasi. *will rise* mengubah kemungkinan jadi prediksi: maknanya berubah. Pilihan terakhir menyalin sumbernya kata per kata tanpa tanda kutip dan tanpa sitasi.

blocks.text:
**Citing** (*menyitasi*) means telling the reader where an idea or a quote comes from. Academic writing does it in two places:
1. **In the text** (*sitasi dalam teks*), right where you use the idea: the author's **family name** and the **year**.
2. In a **reference list** (*daftar pustaka*) at the end: full details of every source you cited, in alphabetical order by family name.

There are several citation styles: **APA** (common in the social sciences, education and psychology, and used by many Indonesian universities and journals), **Harvard**, **MLA**, **Chicago** and **IEEE** (numbers, common in engineering). The idea is the same; the details differ. Here we use **APA, 7th edition** as one common example: always follow the style your university, department or journal asks for.

**APA in the text:**
- at the end of the sentence: *… (Santoso, 2021).*
- with the name in your sentence: *Santoso (2021) found that …*
- two authors: *(Pratama & Lestari, 2022)* / *Pratama and Lestari (2022)*; three or more: *(Hidayat et al., 2020)* (*et al.* = dan kawan-kawan)
- a quote also needs the page: *(Santoso, 2021, p. 34)*

**APA in the reference list** (a book): *Santoso, B. (2021). Young workers in the city. Nusantara Press.* Family name, initial, (year), title (in italics), publisher. A journal article also gives the journal name, volume, issue, pages and usually a DOI link.

**Reporting verbs** (*kata kerja pelapor*) introduce a source and show how the author makes the claim:
- **argues**: gives reasons for a view
- **claims**: says it is true (can sound as if you doubt it)
- **states / notes**: neutral
- **suggests**: a careful conclusion (as in the hedging lesson)
- **found / reports**: the results of research
- **points out**: something true that you accept
APA usually uses the past tense for what a study found (*Hidayat et al. (2020) found that …*); many writers use the present for views (*Santoso argues that …*). Choose one and be consistent.

id.text:
**Menyitasi** (*citing*) artinya memberi tahu pembaca dari mana sebuah ide atau kutipan berasal. Tulisan akademik melakukannya di dua tempat:
1. **Di dalam teks** (sitasi dalam teks), tepat di tempat kamu memakai idenya: **nama keluarga** penulis dan **tahunnya**.
2. Di **daftar pustaka** (*reference list*) di akhir: detail lengkap setiap sumber yang kamu sitasi, diurutkan menurut abjad nama keluarga.

Ada beberapa gaya sitasi: **APA** (umum di ilmu sosial, pendidikan dan psikologi, dan dipakai banyak universitas dan jurnal di Indonesia), **Harvard**, **MLA**, **Chicago** dan **IEEE** (pakai nomor, umum di teknik). Idenya sama; detailnya berbeda. Di sini kita memakai **APA edisi ke-7** sebagai salah satu contoh yang umum: selalu ikuti gaya yang diminta universitas, jurusan atau jurnalmu.

**APA di dalam teks:**
- di akhir kalimat: *… (Santoso, 2021).*
- dengan nama di dalam kalimatmu: *Santoso (2021) found that …*
- dua penulis: *(Pratama & Lestari, 2022)* / *Pratama and Lestari (2022)*; tiga atau lebih: *(Hidayat et al., 2020)* (*et al.* = dan kawan-kawan)
- kutipan langsung juga butuh halaman: *(Santoso, 2021, p. 34)*

**APA di daftar pustaka** (buku): *Santoso, B. (2021). Young workers in the city. Nusantara Press.* Nama keluarga, inisial, (tahun), judul (miring), penerbit. Artikel jurnal juga mencantumkan nama jurnal, volume, nomor, halaman dan biasanya tautan DOI.

**Kata kerja pelapor** (*reporting verbs*) memperkenalkan sumber dan menunjukkan bagaimana penulisnya menyampaikan klaim:
- **argues**: memberi alasan untuk sebuah pandangan
- **claims**: menyatakan sesuatu benar (bisa terdengar seolah kamu meragukannya)
- **states / notes**: netral
- **suggests**: kesimpulan yang hati-hati (seperti di pelajaran hedging)
- **found / reports**: hasil penelitian
- **points out**: sesuatu yang benar dan kamu terima
APA biasanya memakai bentuk lampau untuk temuan penelitian (*Hidayat et al. (2020) found that …*); banyak penulis memakai bentuk sekarang untuk pandangan (*Santoso argues that …*). Pilih satu dan konsisten.

rows.id: Pekerja jarak jauh cenderung melaporkan kepuasan kerja yang lebih tinggi (Pratama & Lestari, 2022).

blocks.prompt: Budi copies this sentence from a report into his thesis and adds a citation, but no quotation marks: 'Flooding poses a serious threat to coastal communities in northern Java (Wibowo, 2023).' Is this acceptable?
options: Yes, because he gave the author and the year.
No: he must either put the copied words in quotation marks or paraphrase them.
Yes, as long as the sentence is shorter than 20 words.
blocks.explain: The citation credits Wibowo's **idea**, but the **words** are still Wibowo's: without quotation marks, it looks as if Budi wrote them. He must quote them ("…" + the page) or paraphrase them properly. There's no 'safe' number of words you can copy.

id.prompt: Budi menyalin kalimat ini dari sebuah laporan ke skripsinya dan menambahkan sitasi, tapi tanpa tanda kutip: 'Flooding poses a serious threat to coastal communities in northern Java (Wibowo, 2023).' Apakah ini boleh?
id.explain: Sitasinya mengakui **ide** Wibowo, tapi **kata-katanya** tetap milik Wibowo: tanpa tanda kutip, kelihatannya Budi yang menulisnya. Dia harus mengutipnya ("…" + halamannya) atau memparafrasekannya dengan benar. Tidak ada jumlah kata yang 'aman' untuk disalin.

material.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: the four criteria and band 7

id.title: IELTS Writing Task 2: empat kriteria dan band 7

blocks.text:
**The task (a recap from B2):** an essay of **at least 250 words** in about **40 minutes**, the same kind of task in IELTS Academic and General Training. Task 2 carries more weight in your Writing score than Task 1. The question types, using teachers' names (not official ones):
- **opinion**: *To what extent do you agree or disagree?*
- **discussion**: *Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.*
- **problem–solution**: *What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?* (or causes and solutions)
- **advantages–disadvantages**: *Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?* (this one needs your view on which side is bigger)
- **two-part** (direct questions): *Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?* Answer **both** questions.

**The four criteria.** Examiners score Task 2 on four criteria (*kriteria*), each worth **25%**:
1. **Task Response**: Did you answer every part of the question, with a clear position and ideas that are developed and supported?
2. **Coherence and Cohesion**: Is it logically organised, with clear paragraphs, and linkers and reference words (*this, they, such*) that help the reader?
3. **Lexical Resource** (*lexical* = tentang kosakata): the range, precision and accuracy of your vocabulary, including collocations and spelling.
4. **Grammatical Range and Accuracy**: a variety of structures (simple and complex sentences), used accurately, with correct punctuation.

**Band 7 in plain words** (from the public band descriptors, updated in 2023):
- **Task Response**: the main parts of the question are answered; a **clear position** that you develop; main ideas extended and supported (a weakness still allowed at 7: over-generalising, or support that isn't always focused).
- **Coherence and Cohesion**: ideas logically organised with **clear progression**; a range of linkers and reference words used flexibly (some over- or under-use is OK); paragraphs generally work well.
- **Lexical Resource**: enough vocabulary for some flexibility and precision; **some less common words** or idiomatic items; awareness of style and collocation; only a few spelling or word-formation errors.
- **Grammatical Range and Accuracy**: **a variety of complex structures**; grammar and punctuation generally well controlled; **error-free sentences are frequent**.
Band 7 is not 'perfect': a few mistakes are expected.

**What costs marks:** fewer than 250 words; not answering every part; essays that are partly or wholly plagiarised or memorised; bullet points or notes instead of full paragraphs. Words copied straight from the question get no credit, so paraphrase it.

id.text:
**Tugasnya (ulasan dari B2):** esai **minimal 250 kata** dalam sekitar **40 menit**, jenis tugas yang sama di IELTS Academic dan General Training. Bobot Task 2 dalam skor Writing-mu lebih besar daripada Task 1. Tipe-tipe pertanyaannya, dengan nama yang dipakai guru (bukan nama resmi):
- **opini**: *To what extent do you agree or disagree?*
- **diskusi**: *Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.*
- **masalah–solusi**: *What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?* (atau penyebab dan solusi)
- **kelebihan–kekurangan**: *Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?* (yang ini butuh pandanganmu tentang sisi mana yang lebih besar)
- **dua pertanyaan** (pertanyaan langsung): *Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?* Jawab **kedua** pertanyaannya.

**Empat kriteria.** Penguji menilai Task 2 dengan empat kriteria, masing-masing bernilai **25%**:
1. **Task Response**: Apakah kamu menjawab setiap bagian pertanyaan, dengan posisi yang jelas dan ide yang dikembangkan dan didukung?
2. **Coherence and Cohesion**: Apakah susunannya logis, dengan paragraf yang jelas, serta kata penghubung dan kata rujukan (*this, they, such*) yang membantu pembaca?
3. **Lexical Resource** (*lexical* = tentang kosakata): keragaman, ketepatan dan kebenaran kosakatamu, termasuk kolokasi dan ejaan.
4. **Grammatical Range and Accuracy**: variasi struktur (kalimat sederhana dan kompleks), dipakai dengan tepat, dengan tanda baca yang benar.

**Band 7 dengan bahasa sederhana** (dari band descriptors publik, diperbarui tahun 2023):
- **Task Response**: bagian-bagian utama pertanyaan dijawab; **posisi yang jelas** dan kamu kembangkan; ide pokok diperluas dan didukung (kelemahan yang masih dibolehkan di 7: terlalu menggeneralisasi, atau dukungan yang tidak selalu fokus).
- **Coherence and Cohesion**: ide tersusun logis dengan **alur yang jelas**; berbagai kata penghubung dan kata rujukan dipakai dengan luwes (sedikit terlalu banyak atau terlalu sedikit masih oke); paragrafnya umumnya berfungsi dengan baik.
- **Lexical Resource**: kosakata cukup untuk sedikit keluwesan dan ketepatan; **beberapa kata yang kurang umum** atau ungkapan idiomatis; kesadaran akan gaya dan kolokasi; hanya sedikit kesalahan ejaan atau pembentukan kata.
- **Grammatical Range and Accuracy**: **variasi struktur kalimat kompleks**; tata bahasa dan tanda baca umumnya terkendali dengan baik; **kalimat yang bebas kesalahan sering muncul**.
Band 7 bukan berarti 'sempurna': beberapa kesalahan itu wajar.

**Yang mengurangi nilai:** kurang dari 250 kata; tidak menjawab setiap bagian; esai yang sebagian atau seluruhnya hasil plagiat atau hafalan; poin-poin (bullet) atau catatan, bukan paragraf utuh. Kata-kata yang disalin langsung dari pertanyaan tidak dihitung, jadi parafrasekan pertanyaannya.

rows.en: The essay never says whether the writer agrees or disagrees.
rows.id: Esai itu tidak pernah menyatakan apakah penulisnya setuju atau tidak setuju.

rows.id: Satu paragraf melompat-lompat di antara tiga topik berbeda, dan 'Moreover' dipakai untuk menjawab sisi sebaliknya.

rows.id: Kebanyakan kalimatnya pendek dan sederhana, dan beberapa kalimat panjangnya punya kesalahan bentuk kata kerja.

blocks.text:
**Plan before you write** (about 5 minutes): your position, one main idea per body paragraph, and the counter-argument you'll answer. Then about 30 minutes to write and 5 to check: does each paragraph start with its point? Is every part of the question answered? At least 250 words?

**Support without sources.** In IELTS you can't look anything up, so support ideas with reasons and general examples (*in many Indonesian cities, …*). A made-up precise statistic (*78.3% of Indonesians …*) doesn't make an essay more convincing; a clear, relevant example does.

id.text:
**Rencanakan sebelum menulis** (sekitar 5 menit): posisimu, satu ide pokok per paragraf isi, dan kontra-argumen yang akan kamu jawab. Lalu sekitar 30 menit menulis dan 5 menit memeriksa: apakah setiap paragraf dimulai dengan intinya? Apakah setiap bagian pertanyaan sudah dijawab? Minimal 250 kata?

**Mendukung tanpa sumber.** Di IELTS kamu tidak bisa mencari apa pun, jadi dukung idemu dengan alasan dan contoh umum (*in many Indonesian cities, …*). Statistik karangan yang sangat persis (*78.3% of Indonesians …*) tidak membuat esai lebih meyakinkan; contoh yang jelas dan relevan yang membuatnya meyakinkan.

blocks.prompt: An IELTS question: 'More people are moving from villages to big cities. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?' What must the essay do?
options: Answer both questions: the reasons, and whether it is positive or negative.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of village life.
Give only the writer's opinion on whether it is positive or negative.
blocks.explain: This is a **two-part** question: each question is a part of the task. Leaving one out, or writing about a different topic (village life in general), weakens **Task Response**. Plan one body paragraph for the reasons and one for your view.

id.prompt: Sebuah pertanyaan IELTS: 'More people are moving from villages to big cities. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?' Apa yang harus dilakukan esainya?
id.explain: Ini pertanyaan **dua bagian**: setiap pertanyaan adalah bagian dari tugasnya. Melewatkan salah satunya, atau menulis tentang topik lain (kehidupan desa secara umum), melemahkan **Task Response**. Rencanakan satu paragraf isi untuk alasannya dan satu untuk pandanganmu.

flashcards.back: thesis statement: your answer to the question in one sentence (I largely agree, because …)
topic sentence → explanation → example / evidence → link back to the thesis
rebuttal (This argument has some merit, but … / However, this view overlooks …)
paraphrase: new words AND new structure, the same meaning, still cited
a quote: the exact words in quotation marks + (Author, year, p. x)
reference list: full details of every source, A–Z by family name

resources.title: Paraphrase: Write It in Your Own Words
resources.note: A short guide for university students: what a paraphrase is, six steps for writing one (reread, set the original aside, write, compare, put borrowed phrases in quotation marks, record the source), and an original passage compared with a good paraphrase and a plagiarised one. In English.

id.note: Panduan singkat untuk mahasiswa: apa itu parafrase, enam langkah menulisnya (baca ulang, singkirkan teks aslinya, tulis, bandingkan, beri tanda kutip pada frasa yang dipinjam, catat sumbernya), dan perbandingan teks asli dengan parafrase yang baik dan yang plagiat. Dalam bahasa Inggris.

resources.title: In-Text Citations: The Basics (APA 7th edition)
resources.note: APA's author-date citations in the text: (Jones, 1998) and Jones (1998) found …, page numbers for quotes, and citing paraphrases. It goes into more detail than this lesson (titles, long quotes, sources without page numbers). In English.

id.note: Sitasi dalam teks gaya APA (penulis-tahun): (Jones, 1998) dan Jones (1998) found …, nomor halaman untuk kutipan, dan menyitasi parafrase. Lebih rinci daripada pelajaran ini (judul, kutipan panjang, sumber tanpa nomor halaman). Dalam bahasa Inggris.

id.note: Halaman resmi tentang cara penilaian IELTS Writing: tautan ke band descriptors Writing lengkap (PDF), kriteria penilaian utama, dan video singkat untuk setiap kriteria (Task Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy). Dalam bahasa Inggris.

id.intro: Di B2 kamu sudah menulis esai utuh dengan thesis, paragraf isi dan penutup. Sekarang kamu akan membuat argumen yang benar-benar **koheren**, memakai ide penulis lain dengan jujur (**memparafrasekan, mengutip dan menyitasinya**), dan melihat persis apa yang dibutuhkan esai **IELTS Writing Task 2** untuk band 7. Semua alat C1-mu (hedging, kolokasi dan nominalisasi) bertemu di sini.
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya esai C1 dengan esai yang saya tulis di B2?
Berapa kata yang boleh saya salin dari sumber sebelum dianggap plagiarisme?
Apakah esai IELTS Task 2 perlu daftar pustaka?

assessment.aw-1: Paragraf isi ini berasal dari esai yang berpendapat bahwa kota sebaiknya menanam lebih banyak pohon. Kalimat mana yang melanggar aturan 'satu ide pokok' dan sebaiknya dihapus? Tulis nomornya. (1) Trees can make city streets noticeably cooler. (2) Their shade blocks direct sunlight, so roads and buildings absorb less heat. (3) Many residents of Surabaya also enjoy jogging in the city's parks in the morning. (4) For example, tree-lined streets in Surabaya tend to feel much cooler on hot afternoons than open roads nearby. (5) Planting more trees is therefore one of the cheapest ways to make a city more comfortable.
assessment.aw-2: Dalam esai argumentatif, penulis lebih dulu menyampaikan pandangan terkuat yang berlawanan dengan posisinya. Apa nama jawaban penulis terhadap pandangan itu, bagian yang menunjukkan kenapa pandangan itu lebih lemah? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.aw-3: Esai Rina diakhiri dengan entri daftar pustaka APA ini untuk sebuah artikel jurnal. Ada satu bagian penting yang hilang. Apa itu? Jawab dalam bahasa Inggris. 'Pratama, A. Remote work and job satisfaction in Jakarta. Indonesian Journal of Work Studies, 12(2), 45–60. https://doi.org/10.1234/ijws.12.2.45'
assessment.aw-4: Lengkapi parafrasenya dengan SATU kata benda. Sumber: 'House prices in Bali rose sharply between 2015 and 2020' (Putra, 2021). Parafrase: 'Putra (2021) reports a sharp ___ in Balinese house prices between 2015 and 2020.'
assessment.aw-5: Sari ingin memakai enam kata persis dari sebuah laporan di skripsinya, beserta sitasi dan nomor halamannya. Tanda baca apa yang harus mengapit kata-kata itu? Tulis dua kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.aw-6: Komentar penguji tentang esai IELTS Writing Task 2 Budi: 'Wide range of vocabulary, accurate complex sentences and clear paragraphs. However, the question asked whether the advantages of online shopping outweigh the disadvantages, and the essay only lists advantages and never gives the writer's view.' Kriteria mana dari empat kriteria yang paling terpengaruh oleh kelemahan ini? Tulis namanya dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.aw-7: Dimas menulis esai IELTS Writing Task 2 sebanyak 231 kata. Minimal berapa kata lagi yang dia butuhkan untuk mencapai panjang minimum? Tulis angkanya.
